content: This document outlines an example of HIV case surveillance reporting mandates as specified under Title 22, Chapter 250 of the Maine Revised Statutes, which governs the control of notifiable diseases and conditions. The State of Maine asserts copyright over its codified statutes. If this material is republished, the State requires the inclusion of a disclaimer acknowledging that all copyrights and other rights to the statutory text are reserved by the State of Maine. The text reflects updates made through the First Regular Session of the 123rd Legislature and is current as of December 31, 2007, but it is subject to change without notice. It is important to note that this version has not been officially certified by the Secretary of State. For certified text, one should refer to the Maine Revised Statutes Annotated and its supplements. The Office of the Revisor of Statutes requests that any statutory publication produced using this material be shared with them. This request is not intended to restrict publishing activities but to track publications, avoid unnecessary duplication, and preserve the State's copyright rights. Additionally, the Revisor's Office does not provide legal advice, research, or interpretation of Maine law to the public. For legal assistance, individuals are advised to consult a qualified attorney. The document also includes a detailed table of contents for the statutory sections related to public health, including definitions, rules, penalties, inspections, and the general authority of the department. There are also provisions for extreme public health emergencies and mandatory blood-borne pathogen testing, including judicial consent and confidentiality. Notably, a section on HIV counseling has been repealed.
